text:
alex: heads-up — profiler shows ~18% tail-latency regression on 8xA100 when we enable KV-shard-by-layer with TP+PP. noticed during nightly perf-run.
maria: ugh, when did this start? did the kernel selection change in the runtime build? :eyes:
alex: regression introduced after 2025-11-02 runtime patch that added a new GEMM kernel path for int8 fused attention. perf pipe shows different kernel being chosen for certain sequence lengths when KV is sharded across TP.
kevin: can you paste the profiler output? quick numbers are fine.
alex: sure — from the perf run (repro command below)

# repro command
./run_perf.sh --model gpt-60b --config configs/8x-a100-tp2-pp4-kvshard.json --seq 1024 --batch 1 --iters 200

alex: hotpath breakdown (median tokens/ms):
- attention-gemm: 0.42 -> 0.51 (TP+KV-shard)
- all-reduce (kv): 0.08 -> 0.18
- kv-serialize: 0.03 -> 0.06
- compute-overlap lost: ~0.15 tokens/ms
maria: so all-reduce is the big jump. looks like we’re not overlapping comm when shard placement crosses TP partitions.
jon: do we shard KV by tensor-parallel rank or by pipeline stage? current heur is by "layer owner" so it maps to PP owner which may scatter across TP groups.
sara: that mapping was chosen to keep local KV locality for PP hot layers, but maybe for TP-heavy configs it causes extra cross-node all-reduces.
kevin: timeline: before change KV was replicated per-GPU (DP-ish) -> low all-reduce but higher memory. after change we experimented with layer-owner sharding to save mem.
alex: exactly. memory drop is ~25% which is great, but perf hit on TP+PP combos is problematic.
maria: can we try alternate sharding heuristics quickly? two quick ideas:
  1) TP-affine sharding: shard across TP ranks inside each PP stage (minimizes inter-TP comm).
  2) Hybrid split: replicate critical hot KV layers (first N) and shard colder layers.
jon: also check kernel selection: new int8 fused GEMM has worse comm-compute overlap because it batches differently. maybe if kernel emits larger cooperative launches, it delays NVLink progress engine.
kevin: good call. @alex can you re-run with env var to force old kernel path? i.e. RUNTIME_USE_LEGACY_GEMM=1
alex: just did. results: tail-latency improved to +6% (vs +18% before). all-reduce still up but smaller.
alex: logs: when legacy kernel chosen, attention kernel time 0.44, all-reduce 0.10.
sara: that suggests interaction between kernel micro-batching and our async all-reduce progress. the new kernel probably increases compute chunk size so NCCL progress can't interleave.
maria: short-term mitigation: revert auto-switch for TP+PP configs or add rule to force legacy GEMM if KV_shard == layer-owner and TP>1.
kevin: long-term: we should implement TP-affine sharding and a heuristic that picks replica/replicate for first K layers. also look at making NCCL progress explicit (progress thread) for these kernels.
jon: we also need more fine-grained traces (per-kernel CUDA events + NCCL op timestamps) for a few representative sequences (256/512/1024).
alex: I'll open a perf task with hypothesis, repro, and initial data. provisional plan: (1) quick revert rule in runtime (2) run TP-affine experiment (3) add traces. anyone want to pair on TP-affine mapping?
sara: I can pair tomorrow AM.
maria: assign to alex+kevin+sara. add to release-blocking if we can't get perf within 10% of baseline.
deploy-bot: dev cluster patch 2025-11-07-rc3 deployed to perf-runner-3 :rocket:
kevin: thanks. alex — drop the perf artifacts in the task and ping #eng-runtime when done. add the small repro script to help SRE run tests.
alex: will do. creating task now. :thumbsup:
